method: python3 over scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json + quran-verses.json (particle POS/LEM, person/gender/number features, grammatical number, word order); node scripts/cross_reference_tafsir.mjs on 5:6, 16:112, 10:22, 5:64; overlap greps against content/tadabbur/

results.notes: SUBSTRATE CONFIRMED: 5:6:4:1 is idha tagged T (temporal, LEM:idha) governing qumtum ila al-salah; 5:6:18:2 and 5:6:22:2 are both in tagged COND (LEM:in) governing junuban and marda/safar. Two distinct particles in one ayah, mechanically verified. GROUNDING GAP: none of the four pulled sources (Tabari, Jalalayn, Ibn Kathir, Muyassar) note the particle-force distinction; Tabari's ikhtilaf on idha qumtum concerns WHICH occasions of standing it covers, not idha-certainty vs in-contingency — the candidate's claim that this ikhtilaf 'turns on the particle's force' overstates it. The Abu Hayyan / al-Alusi attributions could not be verified with available tools; either verify them independently before publishing or attribute generically to 'standard classical nahw' (the idha/in doctrine itself is uncontroversial). OVERLAP CLAIM FALSE: content/tadabbur/005-al-maidah/ exists with ~70 files, including ayah-006.md directly on this verse. That file walks both phrases (idha qumtum, wa in kuntum junuban) but never makes the particle point, so the angle is still fresh — but the pitch's 'whole surah uncovered' framing must be corrected.
results.corrected: Keep the reveal, reframed: (a) overlap note becomes 'fresh grammatical angle on 5:6, which content/tadabbur/005-al-maidah/ayah-006.md already covers without the idha/in point'; (b) ground the particle distinction in standard classical nahw generally, citing Abu Hayyan/al-Alusi only after independent verification; (c) drop the claim that Tabari's ikhtilaf turns on the particle's force; (d) keep the 'worship is the default rhythm' payoff explicitly flagged as reflective reading, not a classical or fiqh claim.

results.notes: SUBSTRATE CONFIRMED: 2:155 has al-khawf (2:155:4:2) before al-ju' (2:155:5:3) in a bala' context (wa-la-nabluwannakum); 16:112 has al-ju' (16:112:20:2) before al-khawf (16:112:21:3) in a punishment context (qaryah aminah, rizquha raghadan, fa-kafarat bi-an'um Allah, fa-adhaqaha). Both orders and contexts mechanically verified. TWO HEDGES REQUIRED: (1) The al-Razi/al-Alusi attribution for the cross-verse order comparison is unverified with available tools; pulled sources give context only. Worse, al-Jalalayn supplies a rival, purely historical explanation for the 16:112 order: hunger = the seven-year famine, fear = the Prophet's expeditions — i.e., hunger simply came first chronologically. The 'order tracks test-vs-punishment' reading must be offered as suggestive reflection, not as the established reason for the order. (2) OVERLAP CLAIM PARTLY WRONG: content/tadabbur/002-al-baqarah/ayahs-153-157.md DOES discuss the 2:155 sequence (line 157: 'The sequence moves from emotional (fear) to physical (hunger) to material...'), so 'neither notes the order' is false on the Baqarah side; and 016-an-nahl/ayahs-112-119.md already runs its own reversal analysis (provision from every place -> fear from every place). The genuinely fresh element is only the CROSS-VERSE mirror between the two ayahs, which neither file makes.
results.corrected: Reframe as: 'Two verses pair fear and hunger in opposite order. The contexts (test vs punishment) are explicit in classical tafsir; the punishment verse's hunger-first order also matches recorded history (Jalalayn: seven-year famine, then fear of the expeditions). A further reflective reading — a trial of faith opens with the inner wound while a punishment for ingratitude strikes first at the denied blessing — is offered as modern balagha-style reflection, not classical commentary, unless the al-Razi/al-Alusi citations are independently verified.' Downgrade 'the reversal tracks whether you are being refined or judged' from rule (n=2) to suggestive observation, and fix the overlap note to acknowledge both existing files (the fresh contribution is the cross-verse mirror only).

results.notes: SUBSTRATE CONFIRMED: 10:22 opens 2MP (yusayyiru-KUM 10:22:3:2 PRON|2MP; kun-TUM 10:22:9:2 2MP), shifts to 3rd person at the good wind (bi-HIM 10:22:13:2 PRON|3MP; farih-U 10:22:16 3MP; jarayna is 3FP of the ships), and the storm's second person is inside the sailors' quoted du'a (anjay-TA 10:22:36:2 PERF|2MS addressed to God, -NA 1P). All person values read directly from features. GROUNDING STRONG: al-Jalalayn — one of the four sources actually pulled — explicitly annotates wa-jarayna bihim with 'fihi iltifat an al-khitab' (an iltifat away from direct address). The classical tradition demonstrably saw this exact turn in this exact verse; the Zamakhshari/Kashshaf textbook-example claim is consistent with that. OVERLAP VERIFIED: content/tadabbur/010-yunus/ayahs-021-024.md covers the passage but contains no iltifat/person-shift discussion (grep clean). One precision note for the writer: the return to 2nd person is the sailors addressing GOD in quoted prayer, not the narration resuming address to them — the candidate's own wording ('they cry if YOU save US') is accurate; keep that framing and avoid implying the narrative voice snaps back to addressing the sailors.

SUBSTRATE CONFIRMED: 5:64:3:1 yadu = FS (singular, their claim), 5:64:7:1 aydi-him = FP (plural, turned back), 5:64:12:1 yada-hu = FD (dual) with mabsutatani FD — three grammatical numbers on root y-d-y in one verse, mechanically verified. GROUNDING STRONG: al-Jalalayn (pulled) explicitly notes the dual as intensification of generosity: 'thany al-yad li-ifadat al-kathrah, idh ghayat ma yabdhuluhu al-sakhiyy min malihi an yu'tiya bi-yadayhi' — the number-move IS classically observed. Muyassar's al-Jawwad al-Karim gloss also confirms as claimed. The bila-kayf adab note is appropriate and should be kept. SOLE DEFECT — OVERLAP CLAIM FALSE: 'Surah al-Ma'idah has no tadabbur file' is wrong; content/tadabbur/005-al-maidah/ayahs-064-066.md covers this exact verse at length, including the maghlulah->mabsutatan constriction/expansion contrast. It does NOT make the singular->plural->dual number analysis explicit, so the grammatical-number angle remains fresh — but the pitch must be reframed as a new angle on covered content and differentiated from the existing file's contrast reading.
results.corrected: Keep the reveal intact (strongest-grounded of the four after GC-3): classical warrant is in-hand from al-Jalalayn's explicit comment on the dual. Replace the overlap note with: 'content/tadabbur/005-al-maidah/ayahs-064-066.md covers 5:64 and its open/chained contrast but never surfaces the singular/plural/dual number progression — this article's job is the number grammar specifically, cross-linking the existing tadabbur.' Retain the bila-kayf disclaimer on the divine-attribute question.
